title: Topology & Fares Management — each menu option opens its page
preface: This test is to confirm the user can open the Topology & Fares Management module and reach each of its pages from the Topology main menu.
preconds:
**GIVEN** the user is signed into CloudFare with the Dashboard displayed
**AND** the user has rights to the Topology & Fares Management module

steps.content: **WHEN** the user opens the Topology & Fares Management module via the '3 dot' icon to the right of the 'Topology & Fares' text and selects each option on the Topology main menu
steps.expected: **THEN** each selected Topology & Fares page opens

change_note: Grounded the module name to the spec's 'Topology & Fares Management module' and named the '3 dot' Topology main-menu entry point (FBD-100296 §161-162). Title tightened to <Feature> — <observable behaviour>.

title: Topology filter — services and routes filter by operator
preface: This test is to confirm that services and routes can be filtered and managed by operator level within the CloudFare Operator Hierarchy.
preconds:
**GIVEN** the user is in the Topology & Fares Management module
**AND** more than one operator level exists in the CloudFare Operator Hierarchy

steps.content: **WHEN** the user selects an operator level in the hierarchy
steps.expected:
**THEN** only that level's services and routes are shown
**UNCONFIRMED** — a discrete 'filter by operator' control on the Topology & Fares screen is not described in the governing specs; the specs describe an Operator Hierarchy level (FBD-100385 para 178) and a fixed OperatorId of 1 (FBD-100698 para 86). Confirm the actual filter control on the live system.

change_note: Re-expressed 'filter by operator' as selecting an Operator Hierarchy level, the only operator-scoping mechanism found in the specs. The specific filter widget is unverified.
gaps: No governing spec describes a 'filter by operator' control on the Topology & Fares Management screen; only hierarchy levels (FBD-100385 §178).

title: Fares export — configured fares are exported
preface: This test is to confirm the user can export configured fares from CloudFare.
preconds:
**GIVEN** the user is signed into CloudFare
**AND** routes with a shared Service Group have fares configured (e.g. routes sharing one service group)

steps.content: **WHEN** the user runs the fares export (Fares Export function, or exports fares for routes sharing a Service Group)
steps.expected:
**THEN** the fares file is produced
**UNCONFIRMED** — the governing specs place fares export in the Reports module / a dedicated Fares Export function (FBD-100385 para 157-159, detailed in FBD-100336) and describe export for routes sharing a Service Group (FBD-100296 para 241); export 'for a selected operator' from the Topology & Fares page is not confirmed. Confirm the surface and parameters live.

change_note: Fares export exists but is (a) referenced to FBD-100336 and (b) described as service-group based, not per-operator, and not on the Topology & Fares page. Marked the operator/location claims UNCONFIRMED.
gaps: Detailed fares export behaviour lives in FBD-100336 (Fares File Export), which is outside the governing set for this pass.

title: Import Map Point File — stops are added and existing stops updated
preface: This test is to confirm the user can import a map point CSV file to add new stops and update existing stops.
preconds:
**GIVEN** the user is in the Topology & Fares Management module
**AND** a map point CSV file in the specified format is available (see Map Point Import File Example, FBD-100296 ref [1])

steps.content: **WHEN** the user selects 'Import Map Point File' from the Topology main menu, selects the CSV file and presses 'Import'
steps.expected:
**THEN** a success box reports the number of stops added (Stops Added) and updated (Stops Updated)
**AND** stops not already present are added
**AND** existing stops are updated from the file

change_note: Named the exact function ('Import Map Point File'), the Import button, and the success message fields Stops Added / Stops Updated (FBD-100296 §163,167,189,201).

title: Import route data at parent and child operator level
preface: This test is to confirm the user can import route data at parent and child operator level.
preconds: **GIVEN** the user is in the Topology & Fares Management module with an operator selected

steps.content: **WHEN** the user imports route data at parent operator level and at child operator level
steps.expected:
**THEN** the route data is imported at the selected level
**UNCONFIRMED** — the governing spec covers only CSV map-point import and states a TransXChange route import is NOT required during R2.0 (FBD-100296 para 44, para 72); an XLSX route-data import at parent/child level is not described. Confirm this import exists live and capture its real file format and screen.

change_note: Removed the invented 'XLSX' file type from the title/preface. Route-data import at parent/child level is not in the governing spec (route import via TransXChange was deferred). Marked UNCONFIRMED.
gaps: No governing spec describes an XLSX route-data import at parent/child operator level; TransXChange route import was deferred (FBD-100296 §72).

title: Fares rule — a new rule is added

steps.content: **WHEN** the user adds a new fares rule

**THEN** the rule is saved and appears in the configured rules
**UNCONFIRMED** — rules exist and can be exported (Rules Report, FBD-100385 para 125-126), but the governing specs do not describe the add-a-rule screen or fields. Confirm the rule-creation flow live.

change_note: Existence of configurable rules is grounded (Rules Report export, FBD-100385 §125-126); the creation UI is not in the governing set. Marked UNCONFIRMED.
gaps: Rule-creation screen/fields not in the governing specs (only the Rules Report export is).

title: Route Management — create, amend, copy and delete a route
preface: This test is to confirm the user can create, amend, copy and delete a route in the Route Management module. Note: this bundles four behaviours; consider splitting per the Gherkin standard.
preconds: **GIVEN** the user is in the Route Management module with a Service selected in the Services sub-module

steps.content: **WHEN** the user presses 'Create New Route' in the Routes sub-module, completes the route attributes and stops, and presses 'Add Route'
steps.expected: **THEN** the new route is added and appears in the Routes drop-down

steps.content: **WHEN** the user selects the route, opens the '3 dot' menu on the Route Pane and chooses 'Edit Route Attributes' (or 'Copy Route', or 'Delete Route')
steps.expected:
**THEN** 'Edit Route Attributes' applies the amended attributes
**AND** 'Copy Route' creates a copy in the same Service named '<route>-copy'
**AND** 'Delete Route' removes the route after the Yes/No confirmation
**UNCONFIRMED** — that a copied route 'retains its assigned fare area' is not in FBD-100296 (fares are explicitly out of scope of that spec, para 44); confirm fare-area copy behaviour against the fares spec/live.

change_note: Named exact controls: Create New Route / Add Route (§230,257), Copy Route ('-copy', same service) (§261), Edit Route Attributes (§282), Delete Route + Yes/No (§285). Flagged the 'retains fare area' claim as UNCONFIRMED (fares out of scope of FBD-100296).
gaps: Whether a copied route retains its fare area is unverified (fares excluded from FBD-100296).

title: Route — service and public route code configured
preface: This test is to confirm the user can add a route to a Service and set its route codes.
preconds: **GIVEN** the user is in the Route Management module with a Service selected

steps.content: **WHEN** the user sets the route's 'Add to a Service' attribute and its 'Public Route Code' (the code printed on tickets)
steps.expected:
**THEN** the route is saved with the selected Service and Public Route Code
**UNCONFIRMED** — FBD-100296 route attributes are 'Add to a Service' and 'Public Route Code' (para 236-238); there is no per-route 'service code' field nor a per-route 'operator' assignment (routes belong to a Service, not an operator). Confirm what 'service code' and 'operator' mean on the live screen.

change_note: Replaced invented 'service code' and per-route 'operator' with the actual route attributes 'Public Route Code' and 'Add to a Service' (FBD-100296 §236-238). Original labels marked UNCONFIRMED.
gaps: No 'service code' field and no per-route operator assignment in FBD-100296; routes attach to a Service.

title: Route — enable ABT flat fare
preface: This test is to confirm the user can enable ABT flat-fare travel on a route.
preconds: **GIVEN** the user has selected a route in the Route Management module

steps.content: **WHEN** the user enables ABT flat fare on the route
steps.expected:
**THEN** the route is configured for ABT flat-fare travel
**UNCONFIRMED** — an 'ABT flat fare' route attribute is not among the FBD-100296 route attributes (para 234-249), and fares are out of scope of that spec (para 44). Confirm the flat-fare setting exists and where it lives.

change_note: No 'ABT flat fare' attribute in the FBD-100296 route-attribute list; fares out of scope of that spec. Marked UNCONFIRMED.
gaps: 'ABT flat fare' route setting not found in the governing specs.

title: Route — enable Multi-Journey transfers and set the transfer time
preface: This test is to confirm the user can permit Multi-Journey transfers on a route and set the transfer time so a transfer within the window retrieves the correct fare.
preconds: **GIVEN** the user is editing a route's attributes in the Route Management module

steps.content: **WHEN** the user sets the route's 'Transfer Time' (minutes) — and 'Directional Transfer' if the previous journey's direction must match
steps.expected: **THEN** Multi-Journey transfers are permitted on the route with the configured Transfer Time

steps.content: **WHEN** a second tap is made within the configured Transfer Time
steps.expected:
**THEN** the fares engine returns the correct transfer fare for the window
**UNCONFIRMED** — the transfer-fare retrieval is fares-engine behaviour (FBD-100698); confirm the exact fare returned against seeded fares.

change_note: Grounded 'Transfer Time' (minutes) and 'Directional Transfer' as the actual route attributes (FBD-100296 §242,248). The fare-within-window check is fares-engine behaviour and marked UNCONFIRMED.

title: Route — configure the fares triangle and calculate a fare
preface: This test is to confirm the user can configure a route's fares triangle, create a fare area and calculate a fare.
preconds: **GIVEN** the user has selected a route in the Route Management module

steps.content: **WHEN** the user configures the fares triangle, creates a new fare area and calculates a fare
steps.expected:
**THEN** the fares triangle is saved
**AND** the calculated fare matches the configured fare area
**UNCONFIRMED** — fares management (fares triangle, fare areas) is explicitly OUT of scope of FBD-100296 (para 44); the fares-triangle concept is only referenced in passing (para 239). Fare-triangle/area configuration lives in a fares spec (e.g. FBD-100336), outside this governing set. Confirm the screen and fields live.

change_note: Fares-triangle/fare-area configuration is out of scope of the governing route/topology specs. Marked UNCONFIRMED and pointed to the fares spec.
gaps: Fares triangle / fare area configuration not in the governing set (fares excluded from FBD-100296; see FBD-100336).

title: Route — ETM rail substitution service
preface: This test is to confirm the user can create an ETM rail-substitution service route.
preconds: **GIVEN** the user has selected an ETM operator and created a rail replacement service in the Route Management module

steps.content: **WHEN** the user configures the rail-substitute route
steps.expected:
**THEN** the rail-substitute route is saved
**UNCONFIRMED** — 'rail substitution' is grounded as a fare-request concept (tap-on-only taps on an ETM split into tap-on/tap-off by ABT — FBD-100698 para 109), but a CloudFare screen to create a rail-substitution *service route* is not described. Confirm the configuration surface live.

change_note: Rail substitution is grounded as ABT fare-request behaviour (FBD-100698 §109); the route-configuration flow is not in the governing specs. Marked UNCONFIRMED.
gaps: No spec describes configuring a rail-substitution service route in CloudFare; only the ABT fare-request behaviour (FBD-100698 §109).

title: Product — an Excess (open-value) product is configured

change_note: 'Excess' is not a product-type column in FBD-100268; the spec treats it as an open-value ticket configured via Minimum/Maximum Value (§47-48). Grounded to those fields and marked the 'Excess product type' UNCONFIRMED.
gaps: 'Excess' as a named product type is not in FBD-100268 (only Min/Max Value fields for open-value tickets).

title: Zones — a multi-zone stop is a member of each of its travel zones
preface: This test is to confirm that a stop lying within more than one overlapping zone is recorded as a member of each zone, so capping can evaluate it against each zone's cap.
preconds:
**GIVEN** the user is signed into CloudFare with rights to Zone Settings (Settings module > Topology sub-module > Zones)
**AND** a stop that lies within more than one zone (e.g. a 403 (IN) stop within both a Magherafelt Ulsterbus Town Service zone and iLink Zone 4 — Ulsterbus Town Service zones can exist within an iLink zone)

steps.content: **WHEN** the user views the stop's zone membership in Zone Settings
steps.expected: **THEN** the stop is listed as a member of each overlapping zone it falls within

steps.content: **WHEN** a card makes qualifying taps at that stop and the EndOfDay settlement runs
steps.expected:
**THEN** the capping engine evaluates the stop against each of its zones' caps
**UNCONFIRMED** — zone membership is derived from the drawn zone boundaries in Zone Settings (FBD-100229 para 119, 187), NOT configured 'within the capping rules'; the per-zone capping evaluation is capping-engine behaviour not detailed in the governing zone spec. Confirm the settlement outcome against seeded caps.

change_note: Grounded the multi-zone concept (overlapping zones / a stop in multiple zones — §119; Ulsterbus Town Service zones within iLink zones — §182,126). Corrected the surface: zone membership is set in Zone Settings (Settings>Topology>Zones §187) from drawn boundaries, not 'within the capping rules'; removed the unverified 'BusinessRules CreateEdit' claim and marked the capping-evaluation THEN UNCONFIRMED.
gaps: Per-zone capping evaluation at settlement is engine behaviour, not covered by the zone spec.
